verdictStatement: Both v4 SHOULD-FIX findings are repaired exactly as specified, and I verified each by measurement rather than by reading the roster's account of itself. The closed-roster claim now holds: I took a full recursive diff of v4 against v5 and every changed path — /artifact, /version, /basedOn, /reviewGuidance, the added /honestyRepairsFromV4, and the /honestyRepairsFromV2 → /honestyRepairsFromV2Historical rename — is named by basedOn.method, so the sentence 'Every path neither the substantive roster nor succession metadata names is unchanged from v4' is true on the artifact's own bytes. Twenty-two keys are deeply unchanged, including every surface, all fifteen governing sources, lockJoin and bridgesMean. All eighteen recorded digests reproduce. The two advisories below are internal cross-reference hygiene: neither states anything false, neither touches a surface, window, attribution or authority, and neither meets the bar I applied to the v4 findings, which was that the artifact contained a statement false as written. I record them so a successor can close them cheaply, not as a reservation on this acceptance.

advisories.subjectQuote: Attack any silent v2-to-v3 change outside honestyRepairsFromV2 / basedOn.method.
advisories.detail: This delta renamed /honestyRepairsFromV2 to /honestyRepairsFromV2Historical, and item 8 still names the pre-rename key. I resolved every honestyRepairsFrom* reference in the artifact against the keys actually present; this is the only genuine orphan. The other five hits are legitimate: two are the rename statement itself (basedOn.method and honestyRepairsFromV4[1], which must name the old key to describe the rename), and three sit inside historical rosters retained verbatim, where naming the then-current key is the point of retention.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: It is an imperative, not an assertion, so nothing false is stated; the referent is one key away and the rename is explained three times in the same document; and it concerns a delta three generations back. I applied the same grading at v4, where I recorded the parallel schemas.v7 orphan as supporting evidence rather than as an independent SHOULD-FIX — and v5 fixed that one. Promoting this to SHOULD-FIX would apply a stricter bar than the one this successor was asked to clear.
advisories.suggestedFix: Point item 8 at honestyRepairsFromV2Historical, or better, restate items 8, 13 and 14 in the version-free form already used for item 5 — 'Attack any silent predecessor-to-successor path outside the named repair roster / basedOn.method' — so the list stops accumulating one line and one rename liability per generation.

The historical list names /honestyRepairsFromV1Historical and /honestyRepairsFromV2Historical. /honestyRepairsFromV3 — which records the v3-to-v4 delta and is therefore equally superseded now that /honestyRepairsFromV4 exists — appears in none of the three. advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The v4 finding had teeth because the unlabelled roster contained a statement false about the artifact — 'governingSources now digest … current schemas.v7' when v4 cited v9. I checked all four items of /honestyRepairsFromV3 against v5 and every one is still true: the v9 citation, the freeze-and-file-09 application warrant, the succession-metadata classification, and the negative claim. So no falsehood is imported, and the closure sentence is unaffected because that path is measurably unchanged. This is a taxonomy gap, not a misstatement.
advisories.suggestedFix: Rename to /honestyRepairsFromV3Historical at the next successor and add it to the historical list — one rename per generation, which is the rule the artifact is already most of the way to stating.
